metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code (VB6 form file with ADODB database connection and Form_Load entry point) present with a dependency on a persistent data store. Classified as application.
metadata.archetype_justification: The application performs CRUD operations — INSERT statements writing customer data to an Access database. It owns persistent state (the .mdb file). Classified as stateful-crud.

classification_consistency_check.reason: Score 1.18 yields Not Ready band but 11 High findings (not ≥12) maps to Remediation Required tier. This divergence occurs because 20 non-core questions scoring 1 produce Medium (not High) findings, depressing the overall score below 1.5 without generating enough High findings to reach the ≥12 threshold for Not Ready tier.

findings.title: No managed compute — desktop EXE on Windows laptops
findings.description: All compute runs as a Win32 desktop EXE (VB6 runtime) on individual Windows laptops. No server-side compute, no cloud infrastructure, no managed container orchestration, no serverless functions.
findings.gap: No managed compute of any kind. The application has zero cloud presence.
findings.recommendation: Re-platform the application as a web-based service deployed on managed compute (ECS Fargate, App Runner, or Lambda). Requires rewriting in a modern language first.

findings.title: Self-managed Access database on file share
findings.description: Database is a Microsoft Access 2003 .mdb file on a SMB file share with hardcoded password. Monthly corruption events. Nightly DTS/SSIS sync to SQL Server 2012 for reporting.
findings.gap: All databases self-managed on file share. No managed services, no automated operations, no failover.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon Aurora (PostgreSQL or MySQL) or RDS. Use AWS DMS for migration. Eliminate Access .mdb and SQL Server reporting tiers.

findings.title: No workflow orchestration
findings.description: CRM business workflows (customer lifecycle, sales processes) entirely hardcoded in VB6 form event handlers with On Error Resume Next error suppression.
findings.gap: No orchestration — all workflow logic hardcoded in application code with no error handling strategy.
findings.recommendation: When re-platforming, implement AWS Step Functions for multi-step business workflows with explicit error handling and retry policies.

findings.title: No async messaging or streaming
findings.description: No messaging or streaming infrastructure. Synchronous database writes with no event emission. Reporting database sync relies on nightly SSIS batch job instead of event-driven replication.
findings.gap: No messaging where state changes cross system boundaries — reporting sync relies on nightly batch instead of real-time events.
findings.recommendation: When re-platforming, implement EventBridge or SNS/SQS for domain events to enable real-time data propagation.

findings.title: No network security
findings.description: No network security configuration. Desktop app connects directly to SMB file share over flat internal network. No VPC, no subnets, no security groups, no network segmentation.
findings.gap: No network isolation or segmentation. Database accessible to anyone on the network.
findings.recommendation: When migrating to AWS, deploy in VPC with private subnets. Place database in isolated data tier with least-privilege security groups.

findings.title: No API entry point
findings.description: No API entry point exists. Desktop fat-client connects directly to database. No API Gateway, ALB, CloudFront, or service exposure mechanism.
findings.gap: Services exposed directly with no gateway or load balancer.
findings.recommendation: When re-platforming as web application, front the API with Amazon API Gateway with throttling, authentication, and request validation.

findings.title: No auto-scaling
findings.description: No auto-scaling. Static desktop EXE with single file server backend. No elasticity, no capacity management.
findings.gap: No auto-scaling — all capacity statically provisioned.
findings.recommendation: When migrating to managed compute, configure auto-scaling on web tier and enable Aurora auto-scaling for read replicas.

findings.title: No backup and recovery
findings.description: No automated backup configuration. Access .mdb on network share with no backup strategy. Monthly corruption events documented with no mitigation.
findings.gap: No backup configuration; no restore procedure; active data corruption occurring monthly.
findings.recommendation: Immediate: implement file-level backups. Long-term: migrate to Aurora with automated backups, PITR, and cross-region replication.

findings.title: Zero Infrastructure as Code coverage
findings.description: No IaC exists. No Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, Helm, or any infrastructure-as-code. All infrastructure manually created.
findings.gap: No IaC — all infrastructure created manually (ClickOps). 0% coverage.
findings.recommendation: Define all cloud infrastructure in CDK or Terraform from day one. Start with database, networking, and compute as IaC before any application deployment.

findings.title: No CI/CD automation
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline. Compiled on one developer's machine. Deployed by copying EXE to laptops by hand. No pipeline definitions, no build configurations.
findings.gap: No CI/CD — all deployments manual. Single developer as sole build/release point.
findings.recommendation: Establish CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions or CodePipeline + CodeBuild) with automated build, test, and deploy stages as first modernization step.

findings.title: VB6 — no cloud-native tooling
findings.description: Written in Visual Basic 6.0 (unsupported since 2008). No AWS SDK, no cloud-native tooling, no modern framework ecosystem. Requires Windows compatibility shims.
findings.gap: VB6 has no AWS SDK and no cloud-native tooling. Cannot target any AWS compute platform.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite in a modern language with AWS SDK support (TypeScript/Node.js or Python recommended).

findings.title: Tightly-coupled monolith
findings.description: Single VB6 form contains UI, business logic, and data access interleaved in event handlers. No separation of concerns, no modular structure, pervasive shared state.
findings.gap: Tightly-coupled monolith with no clear module boundaries, pervasive shared state.
findings.recommendation: Design new application with clear domain boundaries. Identify bounded contexts and implement as separate modules/services. See Decomposition Strategy.

findings.title: All communication synchronous
findings.description: All communication is synchronous. Desktop app makes synchronous ADODB calls. No async patterns, no message queues, no event-driven flows. UI thread blocks on database operations.
findings.gap: All communication synchronous with no async patterns for cross-service state propagation.
findings.recommendation: When re-platforming, implement async communication for state change propagation (SNS/SQS for domain events). Keep synchronous for user-facing reads.

findings.title: No async long-running process handling
findings.description: All operations synchronous regardless of duration. Database operations execute synchronously on UI thread. On Error Resume Next suppresses timeouts.
findings.gap: All operations synchronous regardless of duration — no background job processing.
findings.recommendation: When re-platforming, implement async job processing for operations over 30 seconds (report generation, bulk imports) using SQS + Lambda or Step Functions.

findings.title: No API versioning
findings.description: No API exists, therefore no versioning strategy. Desktop client connects directly to database with no API layer.
findings.gap: No versioning — no API surface exists.
findings.recommendation: When re-platforming as web service, implement URL path versioning (/v1/customers) from the start.

findings.title: Hardcoded service endpoints
findings.description: Database path hardcoded as compile-time constant: DB_PATH = "S:\CRM\sales.mdb". No dynamic discovery, no environment-based configuration.
findings.gap: All service endpoints hard-coded in application code.
findings.recommendation: When re-platforming, externalize endpoints via environment variables or implement AWS Cloud Map for dynamic discovery.

findings.title: Data locked on file share
findings.description: All data stored on SMB network file share as Access .mdb. Crystal Reports 8.5 for reporting. No managed object storage, no S3, no parsing pipeline. Data locked in proprietary format.
findings.gap: Data on local file systems and legacy storage. Inaccessible for modern analytics or AI.
findings.recommendation: Migrate structured data to Aurora. Store documents/unstructured data in S3 with lifecycle policies.

findings.title: No data access layer
findings.description: Database queries scattered directly in UI event handlers. Raw SQL string construction inline. No repository pattern, no DAO, no ORM, no centralized data access.
findings.gap: Database imports and queries scattered across form modules with no pattern.
findings.recommendation: When re-platforming, implement repository/DAO pattern or ORM. Centralize all database access with parameterized queries.

findings.title: Database engines past EOL
findings.description: Microsoft Access 2003 with Jet OLEDB 4.0 (support ended 2014). SQL Server 2012 (support ended 2022). Both unpatched with no security updates.
findings.gap: Engines at or past EOL. Both Access 2003 and SQL Server 2012 unsupported.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to supported engines: Aurora PostgreSQL/MySQL for primary, Aurora or Redshift for reporting.

findings.title: No encryption at rest
findings.description: No encryption at rest. Access .mdb has weak file-level password (not encryption). Data stored in plaintext on network file share.
findings.gap: No encryption at rest configured. Data in plaintext on file share.
findings.recommendation: When migrating to AWS, enable encryption at rest on all data stores using customer-managed KMS keys with rotation policies.

findings.title: No API authentication
findings.description: No authentication mechanism. Anyone with the EXE can access and modify customer data. Only 'authentication' is possession of the compiled executable.
findings.gap: No API authentication — application open to anyone with the EXE.
findings.recommendation: When re-platforming, implement OAuth2/JWT authentication on all API endpoints using Amazon Cognito.

findings.title: No centralized identity integration
findings.description: No identity provider integration. No login flow, no user management, no identity federation. Environ(USERNAME) reads Windows username without validation.
findings.gap: No authentication at all — no external IdP integration.
findings.recommendation: When re-platforming, integrate with Amazon Cognito (SAML/OIDC federation to enterprise AD) for SSO with RBAC.

findings.title: Hardcoded database password in source
findings.description: Database password hardcoded as plaintext constant: Private Const DB_PW As String = "crm2005pw". Committed to version control, compiled into every EXE copy.
findings.gap: Plaintext credentials in source code. Critical security vulnerability.
findings.recommendation: Immediate: rotate the database password. When migrating to AWS, store all credentials in Secrets Manager with automated rotation.

findings.title: No compute hardening or patching
findings.description: No patching strategy. VB6 runtime unsupported. No vulnerability scanning, no hardened images, no SSM integration.
findings.gap: No patching strategy; no vulnerability scanning. Unsupported runtime.
findings.recommendation: When migrating to AWS, use managed compute (Fargate/Lambda) to eliminate OS patching. Enable Inspector for vulnerability scanning.

findings.title: No application security pipeline
findings.description: No security scanning tools. No CI/CD pipeline to integrate scanning into. Known SQL injection vulnerability undetected. No SAST, no DAST, no dependency scanning.
findings.gap: No security scanning tools configured. No pipeline exists for security validation.
findings.recommendation: When establishing CI/CD, integrate SAST, dependency scanning, and container scanning with security gates blocking on critical findings.

findings.title: No distributed tracing
findings.description: No tracing instrumented. No observability of any kind — no logging framework, no trace IDs, no telemetry. On Error Resume Next suppresses error information.
findings.gap: No distributed tracing. Zero observability into application behavior.
findings.recommendation: When re-platforming, instrument with AWS X-Ray or OpenTelemetry from the start with trace ID propagation.

findings.title: No SLO definitions
findings.description: No SLOs defined. No monitoring, no alarms, no error budget tracking. Known reliability issues documented without targets.
findings.gap: No SLOs — no formal definition of acceptable service levels.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for re-platformed application covering availability, latency, and error rate. Implement CloudWatch monitoring.

findings.title: No business metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics published. No metrics infrastructure, no dashboards, no business KPI tracking.
findings.gap: No custom metrics — no business outcome tracking.
findings.recommendation: When re-platforming, publish business metrics (customers created/day, sales pipeline velocity) alongside infrastructure metrics.

findings.title: No anomaly detection or alerting
findings.description: No alerting configured. No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection. Database corruption events discovered by users, not automated monitoring.
findings.gap: No alerting configured. Failures discovered by users.
findings.recommendation: Configure CloudWatch anomaly detection on error rates and latency with PagerDuty/OpsGenie integration.

findings.title: No integration testing
findings.description: No integration tests. No unit tests. No automated tests of any kind. README states: 'No tests, no build server.'
findings.gap: No integration tests — no automated tests at all. Zero test coverage.
findings.recommendation: Establish testing strategy from day one: unit tests, integration tests, and end-to-end tests for critical user journeys, run in CI on every commit.

findings.title: No observability ownership
findings.description: No observability ownership. No dashboards, no alarms, no SLO definitions, no CODEOWNERS, no team attribution. Zero observability infrastructure.
findings.gap: No observability ownership — monitoring completely absent.
findings.recommendation: Establish per-service dashboards and alarms with named team owners. Define CODEOWNERS including observability configs.

decomposition_strategy.rationale: VB6 has no cloud-native tooling, no AWS SDK, and is a desktop fat-client. Cannot be incrementally decomposed via Strangler Fig without web front-end. Requires re-platform first.
decomposition_strategy.effort_estimate: High — 12-18 months for full re-platform with phased service extraction
